topic: How do elevation-dependent beam divergence and pointing losses influence satellite coverage area for optical ground stations?
consensus_response: Elevation-dependent beam divergence and pointing losses significantly impact satellite coverage area by increasing pointing uncertainties, particularly at sea level due to atmospheric turbulence. This results in a gain loss of up to 20 dB compared to vacuum conditions. The variable data rate concept should be implemented through the data format to enable optimum throughput per link session, as both link distance (free space loss) and atmospheric transmissivity are affected by link elevation. Adaptive Optics systems can mitigate these effects but introduce latency and complexity.
reference_context: Atmospheric turbulence causes beam wandering (dominant effect) and beampreading, increasing pointing uncertainties and gain loss of up to 20 dB at sea level compared to vacuum conditions.
